title: Marshall Plan
summary: In June 1947 US Secretary of State George C. Marshall called for a comprehensive program to rebuild Europe, speaking at Harvard. Congress passed the European Recovery Program in March 1948. Its American aid was applied solely to Western Europe, with funding that would eventually rise to over $12 billion.

as_recorded.calendar: Gregorian calendar, month and year of Congressional passage
as_recorded.value: the bill authorizing the European Recovery Program passed Congress in March 1948

where.modern_name: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States (Harvard University, where the plan was announced in June 1947)
where.historical_name: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States of America

importance.justification: A large US-funded postwar aid program for Western Europe, announced by the Secretary of State and passed by Congress, which shaped the early postwar economic recovery of the region.

sources.title: Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations: Marshall Plan, 1948
